app.name: Julià Regader
app.description: Financial education and personal wealth organization.

home.adminNotice: Manage your clients, sessions and business metrics from the admin panel.

legal.disclaimer: This tool is exclusively for educational and personal organization purposes. It does not constitute financial, tax or investment advice. Decisions are the sole responsibility of the user.

auth.title: Sign in to your account
auth.subtitle: No passwords: we'll send a sign-in link to your email.
auth.linkSentTo: We've sent a link to {{email}}. Open it from this same device to sign in.

pending.title: Your account is pending approval
pending.body: Thanks for signing up. Julià will review your request and grant access shortly. We'll email you once your account is active.

rejected.title: Access request not approved
rejected.body: Your access request hasn't been approved. If you think this is a mistake, please contact Julià directly.

admin.homeBody: Here you'll see the client list, their sessions, and business metrics (coming soon).

empty.title: Not enough data yet
empty.body: Add your income, expenses, assets and liabilities to see your net worth and indicators here.

netWorth.label: Net worth
netWorth.tooltip: The sum of all your assets minus the sum of all your liabilities: what you own minus what you owe.

cashFlow.label: Monthly cash flow
cashFlow.tooltip: The difference between your income and your expenses this month.

savingsRate.label: Savings rate
savingsRate.tooltip: The percentage of this month's income you haven't spent: (income − expenses) ÷ income.

emergencyFund.label: Emergency fund
emergencyFund.tooltip: How many months of your current expenses you could cover using only your liquid assets (cash and accounts).

debtToAssets.label: Debt / Assets
debtToAssets.tooltip: How much debt you have relative to everything you own: total liabilities divided by total assets.

debtToIncome.label: Debt / Income
debtToIncome.tooltip: How much debt you have relative to your monthly income: total liabilities divided by this month's income.

common.empty: You haven't added anything here yet.

income.title: Your income
income.description: Add your income sources, fixed or variable.

expenses.title: Your expenses
expenses.description: Add your regular expenses by category.

assets.title: Your assets
assets.description: Accounts, investments, properties and other things you own.

liabilities.title: Your liabilities
liabilities.description: Mortgage, loans, credit cards or other debts.

summary.title: Your net worth
summary.description: This is what you own minus what you owe, calculated from what you just entered.

strategy.title: Investment strategy
strategy.description: This is your own canvas: define whatever asset classes you want and a target percentage for each. The app never recommends an allocation or a specific instrument — the decision is always yours.
strategy.educationalNote: Notice: this is an organization tool, not advice. No figure here is a recommendation.
strategy.templatesNote: These are just generic starting points by asset class, fully editable. They are not a recommendation for your situation.

goals.title: Financial goals
goals.description: Create savings goals with an amount and a date, and track your progress.

tools.title: Educational tools
tools.description: Generic calculators to understand financial concepts. No result here is a recommendation: the decision is always yours.

compoundInterest.title: Compound interest and projection
compoundInterest.description: Simulates how savings could grow with periodic contributions. It's a general theoretical framework, not a promise of returns.

fire.title: Financial independence (4% rule)
fire.description: A general theoretical framework: how much wealth you'd need to live off returns, per the 4% rule (25 times annual expenses).

debtPayoff.title: Debt payoff: avalanche vs. snowball
debtPayoff.description: Compares two didactic methods for prioritizing payoff of your current debts with a monthly extra.
debtPayoff.noDebts: You haven't added any liabilities yet.

budgetRule.title: 50/30/20 budget
budgetRule.description: Compares your actual spending this month with the suggested split: 50% needs, 30% wants, 20% savings.
budgetRule.noIncome: Add this month's income to see the comparison.

glossary.title: Financial glossary
glossary.description: Concepts explained in general terms, so you can understand the indicators on your dashboard.

netWorth.definition: What you own minus what you owe: the sum of all your assets minus the sum of all your liabilities.

asset.definition: Any item or right with economic value that you own: money in accounts, investments, a home, etc.

liability.definition: Any outstanding debt or payment obligation: a mortgage, a loan, a credit card balance.

diversification.definition: Spreading money across different types of assets so you don't depend on how just one performs.

liquidity.definition: How easily an asset can be turned into available cash without losing value, like cash or a checking account.

compoundInterest.definition: When interest earned also earns interest over time, accelerating the growth of savings or debt.

savingsRate.definition: The percentage of your income you don't spend: (income − expenses) divided by income.

debtRatio.definition: A measure of how much debt you have relative to your assets or your income.

emergencyFund.definition: A cushion of liquid assets meant to cover unexpected expenses, usually measured in months of expenses covered.

fourPercentRule.definition: A theoretical framework estimating you could live off invested wealth by withdrawing 4% a year, meaning you'd need about 25 times your annual expenses.

budget502030.definition: A suggested income split: 50% needs, 30% wants, and 20% savings.
